slides.title:
THE HANDOFF
IS THE BOTTLENECK.
slides.body: The conversation moves. The context, permissions and next action often do not.

rows.label: A lead goes quiet
rows.detail: Someone must recover the history and decide what happens next.

rows.label: An answer needs three systems
rows.detail: A person becomes the copy-and-paste connection between them.

rows.label: A colleague uses a different AI
rows.detail: The team repeats the briefing instead of moving the work forward.

slides.sourceLabel: Our focus: the costly gaps between conversations, systems and teams.

slides.title:

FOLLOW THROUGH.
slides.body: Start with service businesses and outreach teams: turn eligible leads and unfinished quotes into the next useful action.
slides.alt: Illustration of a service professional collaborating with a bot team.
bullets: One request from the person leading the work.
Relevant specialists contribute when needed.
The customer gets a clear next step.
slides.sourceLabel: Illustrative customer workflow; initial market focus.

slides.title:
FROM OUTREACH
TO OUTCOME.
slides.body: “Follow up on approved quotes, answer questions and help interested customers book.”

rows.label: Prepare
rows.detail: Bring together the customer history, quote and approved outreach instructions.

rows.label: Converse
rows.detail: A person or designated bot leads; the team supplies relevant answers and context.

rows.label: Complete
rows.detail: Coordinate a booking or human handoff and update the business record.

rows.label: Continue
rows.detail: Keep the decision and next step available to the team.

slides.sourceLabel: Designed workflow. Each connected action follows the customer’s permissions.

slides.title:
MORE THAN
ANOTHER CALL.
slides.body: Three phones can carry three voices. A shared work system carries the task forward.

rows.label: Shared context
rows.detail: Pass the relevant facts, files and decisions without repeating the briefing.

rows.label: Independent specialists
rows.detail: Bring different assistants, tools and account owners into one authorized task.

rows.label: Continuity
rows.detail: Move between discussion, action and follow-up with an accountable result.

slides.sourceLabel: The value is coordinated work, not the number of voices in the room.

slides.title:
ONE FOUNDATION.
MANY PAYING JOBS.
slides.body: Expand from a repeatable workflow into adjacent business needs.

rows.label: Call centers & sales
rows.detail: Recover warm leads, prepare answers, coordinate appointments and hand off with context.

rows.label: Service & operations
rows.detail: Resolve a request across scheduling, files and customer records.

rows.label: Agencies & client teams
rows.detail: Let each side’s assistants contribute to an agreed task.

rows.label: Building & organizing
rows.detail: Plan, create bots and apps, share work and keep projects moving.

slides.sourceLabel: Target use cases, with outcome and reliability measured in customer pilots.

slides.title:
THE CUSTOMER’S
MATH MATTERS.
slides.body: An illustrative month for a team following up on 500 eligible opportunities.

rows.detail: additional appointments
expected contribution from those appointments
illustrative all-in monthly service price
remaining contribution before extra implementation and review costs

slides.sourceLabel: Scenario, not measured results or published pricing. Per appointment: 75% attendance × 30% close rate × $400 job contribution = $90. Five additional appointments cover the assumed $400 price; conversion lift is not guaranteed.

slides.title:
LOW OVERHEAD.
PRICE FOR VALUE.
slides.body: Keep routine coordination lightweight. Use paid intelligence and voice where they improve the outcome.

rows.label: Coordinate efficiently
rows.detail: Message and data transport need not trigger a new model response at every step.

rows.label: Use specialists selectively
rows.detail: Call on the right bot for a decision, rather than keeping every bot working continuously.

rows.label: Match revenue to usage
rows.detail: Subscriptions cover recurring value; usage charges cover variable services.

slides.sourceLabel: MCP is a protocol, not a free hosted service. Hosting, models, voice, telephony, storage and support remain costs. Production unit costs and margins require measurement.

slides.title:
ONE NETWORK.
MULTIPLE REVENUES.
slides.body: Charge for useful work, distribution and a marketplace that helps creators reach customers.

rows.label: Team subscriptions + usage
rows.detail: Recurring workspaces, collaboration and metered services.

rows.label: Creator sales + platform share
rows.detail: People build bots, sell them and earn through the store.

rows.label: Promoted store placement
rows.detail: Paid, clearly identified discovery for relevant bots and tools.

rows.label: Visible keyboard keys
rows.detail: Sponsored or partner placements at the moment of work.

rows.label: White-label services
rows.detail: Agency and business offerings built on the shared platform.

slides.sourceLabel: Planned revenue streams. Pricing, transaction shares and placement terms will be validated with customers.

slides.title:

IN THE WORKFLOW.

bullets: Creators gain a route to useful adoption.
Customers find and activate the right helpers.
Placement earns value when it produces relevance.
slides.sourceLabel: Paid placements are identified. A placement does not grant access to private data.

slides.title:
WE MARKET IT
BY USING IT.
slides.body: Show a customer’s real workflow, then make it repeatable for the next team.

rows.label: Demonstrate
rows.detail: Start with a service or outreach team and one valuable recurring job.

rows.label: Measure
rows.detail: Track completion, booked next steps, review effort and actual service costs.

rows.label: Expand
rows.detail: Invite the customer’s colleagues, partners and their existing bot teams.

rows.label: Distribute
rows.detail: Use creators, agencies, keyboard discovery and white-label partners.

slides.sourceLabel: Adoption thesis: more useful connections can create more reasons to return.

slides.title:
THE NETWORK
GETS MORE USEFUL.
slides.body: The long-term opportunity is a durable place for bot identity, relationships, work and distribution.
slides.alt: Illustration of a connected bot network in a white glass city.
bullets: Handles and contact relationships that persist.
A workspace close to everyday actions.
A marketplace linking creators and customers.
slides.sourceLabel: The defensibility thesis depends on adoption, retention and execution; identifiers alone are not a moat.

slides.title:
FOUNDATIONS
INTO A PRODUCT.
slides.body: Early supervised development demonstrations include bot-to-bot messages, a small file exchange and a shared human-and-assistant voice conversation.

rows.label: Connect
rows.detail: Make accounts, contacts, voice, shared data and rules work together reliably.

rows.label: Complete the experience
rows.detail: Deliver BotBar and BotBoard with the visual quality and independent usability shown here.

rows.label: Extend
rows.detail: Add Zoom, Teams and optional telephone access through supported integrations.

rows.label: Grow
rows.detail: Build creation, store, PC, device connections and additional form factors.

slides.sourceLabel: This book presents the product direction. It is not a claim that every illustrated workflow or integration is already available.
